newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate falls to 11.8 vs 12.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate falls to 11.8 vs 12.7 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate fell to 11.8 percent on Friday amid slight trimming of term rates in bustling end-of-week trade from Thursday's 12.7 percent.
Dealers reported 64.75 million kuna deals, of which just under 50 million were in fresh settlements, with creditors offering another 20 million kuna which found no buyers.
Bank borrowers were also busy repaying old loans ahead of a central bank intervention to help liquidity. The central bank injected 94.5 million kuna in four-day repo funds at an average 8.58 percent.
Interbank rates ranged between call money 11 and 15 percent for 30-day funds, down one percent from earlier this week.
Insurers' charged a steady nine percent for one-week and 13 percent for 30-day loans.

The central bank's kuna mid rates for Saturday and next Monday eased back to 6.0402 versus 5.5992 against the dollar but firmed to 3.5709 from 3.5753 to the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
